{{Elections in Florida}}
The '''2026 United States Senate special election in Florida''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Florida]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] appointee [[Ashley Moody]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] state representative [[Angie Nixon]] are the nominees for their respective parties. The winner will complete the term won in [[2022 United States Senate election in Florida|2022]] by [[Marco Rubio]], who resigned in 2025 to become secretary of state.

After being appointed to the seat, Moody won the Republican nomination against minimal opposition. [[Alex Vindman]], the former director of European Affairs for the [[United States National Security Council|National Security Council]], was considered the Democratic frontrunner and held a significant fundraising advantage during the primary, but Nixon won the nomination with 56.1% of the vote in a major upset.

Democrats have not won a Senate race in Florida since [[2012 United States Senate election in Florida|2012]].

==Background==
[[Marco Rubio]], a U.S. senator from Florida since [[2010 United States Senate election in Florida|2010]], was announced as president-elect [[Donald Trump]]'s nominee for [[United States Secretary of State|Secretary of State]] in November 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Han |first1=Jeongyoon |last2=Grisales |first2=Claudia |title=President-elect Trump nominates Marco Rubio for secretary of state |url=https://www.npr.org/2024/11/11/nx-s1-5187110/donald-trump-marco-rubio-secretary-of-state |access-date=August 23, 2026 |publisher=[[NPR]] |date=November 13, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260823003402/https://www.npr.org/2024/11/11/nx-s1-5187110/donald-trump-marco-rubio-secretary-of-state |archive-date=August 23, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> He was confirmed by the Senate on January 20, 2025 in a 99-0 vote.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Greve |first1=Joan E |title=Senate confirms Marco Rubio as US secretary of state in boost for Trump |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/jan/20/trump-marco-rubio-secretary-of-state |access-date=August 23, 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=January 20, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260823003531/https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/jan/20/trump-marco-rubio-secretary-of-state |archive-date=August 23, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Ashley Moody]], the [[Florida Attorney General|attorney general of Florida]], was named by state governor [[Ron DeSantis]] to fill Rubio's vacant Senate seat, and was sworn in the day after Rubio's confirmation.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Perry |first1=Mitch |title=Ashley Moody sworn in as U.S. senator, while Marco Rubio takes over at State |url=https://floridaphoenix.com/2025/01/21/ashley-moody-sworn-in-as-u-s-senator-while-marco-rubio-takes-over-at-state/ |access-date=August 23, 2026 |work=[[States Newsroom|Florida Phoenix]] |date=January 21, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260823005118/https://floridaphoenix.com/2025/01/21/ashley-moody-sworn-in-as-u-s-senator-while-marco-rubio-takes-over-at-state/ |archive-date=August 23, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Rohrer |first1=Gray |title=From Tallahassee to DC: Ashley Moody sworn in as Florida's newest US senator |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/news/politics/2025/01/22/ashley-moody-us-senate-florida/77873340007/ |access-date=August 23, 2026 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |date=January 22, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260823005001/https://www.tallahassee.com/story/news/politics/2025/01/22/ashley-moody-us-senate-florida/77873340007/ |archive-date=August 23, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Rubio's resignation triggered a [[special election]] for 2026, the next statewide election cycle in Florida. The victor of the special election will serve for the remainder of Rubio's term, until a regular election for a full term in [[2028 United States Senate election in Florida|2028]] is held.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Leonard |first1=Kimberly |title=DeSantis picks Florida AG Ashley Moody to replace Rubio in the Senate |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/01/16/ashley-moody-florida-senator-marco-rubio-replacement-00198643 |access-date=August 23, 2026 |work=[[Politico]] |date=January 16, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250711190055/https://www.politico.com/news/2025/01/16/ashley-moody-florida-senator-marco-rubio-replacement-00198643 |archive-date=July 11, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Hubbard |first1=Kaia |title=What happens to JD Vance's Senate seat and others in Congress selected to join the Trump administration |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/senate-house-special-elections-jd-vance-trump-cabinet/ |access-date=August 23, 2026 |publisher=[[CBS News]] |date=November 13, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260314151600/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/senate-house-special-elections-jd-vance-trump-cabinet/ |archive-date=March 14, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Democratic primary ==
===Campaign===
[[Angie Nixon]], a [[Democratic Party (United States)#Progressives|progressive Democrat]] and a member of the [[Democratic Socialists of America]], won the nomination over [[Alex Vindman]], despite Vindman having amassed $16.3 million in campaign funding compared to Nixon's $975,000.<ref name="NBC Dixon 2026-08-18">{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/angie-nixon-winner-florida-senate-primary-democrat-alex-vindman-moody-rcna593255|title=Democratic socialist Angie Nixon upsets Alex Vindman in Florida's Democratic Senate primary|publisher=NBC News|date=2026-08-18}}</ref><ref name="Guardian Luscombe 2026-08-18">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/18/angie-nixon-alex-vindman-florida-results|title=Democratic socialist Angie Nixon clinches surprise primary win in Florida US Senate race|work=The Guardian|date=2026-08-18}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Peters |first=Cameron |date=2026-09-06 |title=Can Democrats flip Florida in 2026? |url=https://www.vox.com/america-actually/502027/angie-nixon-florida-democratic-senate-nominee-progressive |access-date=2026-09-19 |website=Vox |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Mazzei |first=Patricia |date=2026-09-13 |title=She’s Been Fighting for 20 Years. Has Angie Nixon’s Moment Come? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/13/us/politics/angie-nixon-florida-senate.html |access-date=2026-09-19 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Nixon campaigned on [[universal healthcare]], free [[childcare]], and a national [[rent freeze]].<ref name="Bloomberg Smith 2026-08-18">{{cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-19/progressive-nixon-downs-vindman-in-florida-senate-primary-race|title=Progressive Nixon Downs Vindman in Florida Senate Primary Race|work=Bloomberg|date=2026-08-18}}</ref> Nixon had criticized Vindman for having only recently moved to Florida; Vindman ignored her and attacked the Republican candidate, Moody.<ref name="NBC Dixon 2026-08-18" /> The result was considered a major upset.<ref name="NBC Dixon 2026-08-18" /><ref name="Guardian Luscombe 2026-08-18" />

== General election ==
Formerly a [[swing state]], Florida has shifted increasingly to the Republican Party in recent elections.<ref name="Hubbard-2026">{{cite news |last1=Hubbard |first1=Kaia |title=Florida Senate race set between Ashley Moody and Angie Nixon after projected primary wins |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/florida-senate-primary-results-ashley-moody-angie-nixon/ |access-date=August 22, 2026 |publisher=[[CBS News]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260820215616/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/florida-senate-primary-results-ashley-moody-angie-nixon/ |archive-date=August 20, 2026 |url-status=live |date=August 18, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Peoples-2026">{{cite news |last1=Peoples |first1=Steve |title=Alex Vindman, who testified against Trump during his first impeachment, enters Florida Senate race |url=https://apnews.com/article/alex-vindman-florida-senate-trump-ukraine-impeachment-1850e6e729d1d1efa2ca8baddc47a815 |access-date=August 22, 2026 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 27, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260822233656/https://apnews.com/article/alex-vindman-florida-senate-trump-ukraine-impeachment-1850e6e729d1d1efa2ca8baddc47a815 |archive-date=August 22, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> A Democratic candidate has not won a Senate seat in Florida since [[2012 United States Senate election in Florida|2012]].<ref name="Hubbard-2026" /><ref name="Peoples-2026" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Leonard |first1=Kimberly |title=Florida Dems scramble to regroup after Nixon upset |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/08/19/florida-democrats-nixon-upset-aftermath-01042739 |access-date=August 22, 2026 |work=[[Politico]] |date=August 19, 2026}}</ref> This will be the first U.S. Senate election in Florida where both major party candidates are women.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Matat |first1=Stephany |title=Can Democratic firebrand Angie Nixon win in deep-red Florida? |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/08/19/us-senate-race-pits-nixon-against-moody-whats-next/91362038007/ |access-date=26 August 2026 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |date=August 19, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260826132851/https://www.tallahassee.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/08/19/us-senate-race-pits-nixon-against-moody-whats-next/91362038007/ |archive-date=August 26, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>
